name: Volcanoes and ash
description: Volcano unrest, eruption, ash and lahar products and decisions: Volcano Activity Notices, notices for aviation, alert level and aviation color code badges, ash advisories and lahar warnings. For volcano observatories, emergency managers near volcanoes, schools, airports and utilities.
outsideParties: county emergency management and the sheriff
school districts in the lahar hazard zone
water and power utilities downwind and downstream

glossary.definition: Ground-based hazard level: NORMAL, ADVISORY, WATCH, WARNING.
GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED (or UNASSIGNED) for ash hazard to aircraft. Pairs: NORMAL/GREEN, ADVISORY/YELLOW, WATCH/ORANGE, WARNING/RED.
Volcano Observatory Notice for Aviation: a fixed-line message with the color code, source, summary and cloud height.
Volcanic Ash Advisory from a Volcanic Ash Advisory Center: observed and forecast ash at +6, +12 and +18 hours. It is the basis for SIGMETs.
A volcanic mudflow down a river valley. It can happen with no eruption and arrive in minutes to hours.

productConventions: Always state alert level and color code together, in words. A VONA gives both current and previous color code.
VONA and VAA lines are uppercase fixed labels with UTC times (YYYYMMDD/HHMMZ). Heights are flight levels or feet.
A lahar warning gives a travel time per place.
realismRules: The alert level can go up with no eruption, and down in steps. Observatories do not predict eruption dates.
An ash advisory comes from the VAAC, not the observatory. Airlines act on SIGMETs and the advisory, not on the observatory's alert level alone.
Ash heights above sea level and flight levels differ; do not mix feet and meters in one line.
Lahar evacuation is on foot to high ground, on a timeline set by travel time.
